mainTopic: Leftover חטאות that are left to die or to graze, and the ban on skinning holy animals from the feet
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion about רבי אמי's teaching. Then רבי הושעיא rules that if someone sets aside two חטאות, one as a backup, he brings one and the other grazes. The גמרא asks whose view this follows, rules out the רבנן and רבי שמעון, and concludes it follows רבי, who says a leftover dies only when it replaced a lost animal. It defends this answer against a משנה of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and against the משנה about the יום כיפור goats. Next, a ברייתא about when a leftover חטאת dies is corrected with a קל וחומר: if the animal was lost at the time of כפרה, everyone agrees it dies. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא forbidding skinning from the feet for a בכור and for פסולי המוקדשין. רב חסדא attributes the first rule to בית שמאי and the second to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and three reasons are given for the ban. The amud ends by closing the chapter ולד חטאת.

steps.title: Closing line: what רבי אמי's teaching adds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why רבי אמי needed to state his teaching: we might have thought רבי שמעון's rule applies only to one set of money, and not to two separate sets.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with two sets of money, you might think he does not say this. So רבי אמי teaches us that he does.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final line of the previous discussion. The גמרא is wrapping up why רבי אמי's statement is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought רבי שמעון sends extra money to communal gift offerings only when it all came from one set. A second set set aside as a backup might seem different. רבי אמי teaches that even with two sets, רבי שמעון agrees the extra money goes to communal gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets, here meaning separate sets of money set aside
"He teaches us". The גמרא uses this to show what new point a statement adds

phrases.english: but with two sets, not;
he teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בִּתְרֵי סִדְרֵי לָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion of רבי אמי's teaching
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי אמי, רבי שמעון holds that extra money goes to communal gift offerings even when two separate sets were set aside.

steps.title: Two sin offerings set aside as a backup
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא rules that if someone sets aside two חטאות, one as a backup, he brings one, and the other is left to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הושעיא says: someone who sets aside two sin offerings as a backup gets atonement with one of them, and the other is left to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי הושעיא gives a ruling about a person who set aside an extra חטאת just in case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person meant from the start to bring only one animal. The second was there only in case something happened to the first. רבי הושעיא says the leftover animal is not left to die. It grazes until it gets a blemish, and then it is sold and the money goes to communal gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: As a backup or guarantee, in case the first animal is lost
He gets atonement, by bringing the offering
Grazes, meaning it is left in the pasture until it gets a blemish

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section tries to figure out which opinion this ruling fits.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya says:
one who sets aside two sin offerings as a guarantee,
achieves atonement with one of them,
and the other one grazes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement after the previous discussion ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two חטאות are set aside, one as a backup, one is brought and the other is left to graze.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא רבי הושעיא's ruling follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier opinion this ruling follows. This sets up the next two steps, which test each possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different תנאים hold different rules about when a leftover חטאת dies and when it grazes. The גמרא wants to know which of these opinions רבי הושעיא's ruling fits.

keyTerms.meaning: "According to whom?" This asks which opinion a ruling follows

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the ruling in step 2 follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא (the רבנן, רבי שמעון, or רבי) רבי הושעיא's ruling follows

steps.title: If it follows the רבנן, it is too obvious
steps.stepSummary: The ruling cannot be the view of the רבנן. They already say a leftover grazes in the harder case of an animal set aside to replace a lost one, so a backup case would not need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it follows the רבנן: they already say that when someone sets aside an animal to replace a lost one, it is not treated like the lost one. Do we even need to say this about a backup?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first answer, the רבנן, and rejects it because the ruling would add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the lost-animal case, the רבנן say the extra animal is not left to die; it grazes. A backup animal is an even easier case, since from the start it was only a 'just in case.' So if רבי הושעיא followed the רבנן, his ruling would be obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say". This introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to test
For a lost one, meaning in place of an animal that went missing
"Is it needed?" This means the point is too obvious to need saying

phrases.english: If we say in accordance with the Rabbis,
now, one who sets aside an animal for a lost one,
the Rabbis say it is not considered like the lost one,
is it necessary to state it for a guarantee?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי הושעיא follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר logic: if the רבנן let the leftover graze in the lost-animal case, a backup case is even easier, so the ruling would be unnecessary.

steps.title: If it follows רבי שמעון, the leftover should die
steps.stepSummary: The ruling seems unable to follow רבי שמעון either. He holds that five kinds of חטאות are left to die, so the leftover animal should die rather than graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead, say it follows רבי שמעון. But רבי שמעון said: five sin offerings are left to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second answer, רבי שמעון, and finds a problem right away. His known rule seems to contradict רבי הושעיא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of רבי שמעון's five חטאות that die is a חטאת whose owner already got atonement with another animal. That describes our leftover backup. So by רבי שמעון it should die, while רבי הושעיא says it grazes.

keyTerms.meaning: Five sin offerings that are left to die, a known list of cases

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two sides. The problem with the רבנן is that the ruling would be too obvious. The problem with רבי שמעון is the opposite: the ruling seems to contradict him.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both possible answers now seem to fail, so the גמרא will need a new answer.

phrases.english: Rather, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon;
but didn't Rabbi Shimon say:
five sin offerings are left to die!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבנן option is rejected, tests the רבי שמעון option and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי הושעיא follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון rules that a חטאת whose owner already got atonement is left to die, so a leftover backup animal should die, not graze.

steps.title: רבי הושעיא follows רבי, who limits the rule to a lost animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא's ruling follows רבי. רבי says the leftover dies only in a case of a lost animal, not in a case of a backup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי הושעיא follows רבי. When רבי said the leftover animal dies, he meant only where it replaced a lost animal. But where it was set aside as a backup, it does not die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 3. רבי הושעיא's ruling follows רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says that once a person gains atonement with one חטאת, the leftover one dies. רבי הושעיא teaches that רבי meant this only for an animal set aside to replace a lost one. A backup set aside from the start is different, so it just grazes. That is why רבי הושעיא needed to say his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Loss; a case where the first animal was lost
A backup or guarantee; an extra animal set aside in case the first one is lost

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name after it means רבי יהודה הנשיא. It is not just a general title.

phrases.english: Rather, it follows the view of Rebbi,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here is רבי יהודה הנשיא; רבי הושעיא's ruling follows his view.

phrases.english: when Rebbi said it, it was about a lost animal
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי's rule that the leftover חטאת is left to die.

phrases.english: but about a backup, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבנן and רבי שמעון were both ruled out, the גמרא gives a new answer: רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the ruling to a third תנא and limits that תנא's rule to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think רבי would make even a backup animal die.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי הושעיא teaches that רבי's rule covers only a lost animal, so a backup grazes.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a blemished sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a blemished חטאת is sold and replaced. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says that if the second one was brought first, the first one dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: if someone sets aside a חטאת and it has a blemish, he sells it and brings another in its place. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: if the second one was offered before the first was slaughtered, the first dies, because its owner already gained atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to set up a challenge against Step 6. The challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the first animal was never lost. It was replaced on purpose because of its blemish. Even so, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it dies once the owner gains atonement with the second animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Having a blemish, so the animal cannot be offered
It is left to die
Its owner already gained atonement

phrases.english: We learned: one who sets aside a sin offering,
and it has a blemish
he sells it, and brings another in its place.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
if the second one was offered
before the first one was slaughtered
phrases.notes: The first, blemished animal had been sold. It was going to be slaughtered as regular meat, not as a קרבן.

phrases.english: it shall die, because its owner already gained atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת, וַהֲרֵי הִיא בַּעֲלַת מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be used to attack the answer of Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי limits the death rule to a lost animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a case with no loss where the leftover still dies. The inference comes next.

steps.title: If רבי אלעזר follows רבי, a backup would also die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like רבי. Then רבי would say a leftover dies even when it was a backup.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like רבי. If so, the leftover would die even in a backup case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. If רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows רבי, then רבי does not limit his rule to a lost animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the blemish case nothing was lost, yet the leftover dies. If this is רבי's view, then a backup should also die. That would contradict how Step 6 explained רבי, and רבי הושעיא could not follow רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind, meaning you might assume
He holds

phrases.english: It enters your mind
that Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
holds like Rebbi,
and then even with a backup, it would also die!
phrases.notes: 'It would die' is not written in the text, but the גמרא means it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כְּרַבִּי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the משנה quoted in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 6's claim that רבי holds a backup does not die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reflects רבי, then רבי makes the leftover die even with no loss, so a backup would die too.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אלעזר follows his father, רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is pushed off. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון may hold like his father, רבי שמעון, who says five kinds of חטאות die.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Maybe רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like his father, who said that five kinds of חטאות are left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The משנה may reflect רבי שמעון's view, not רבי's, so it says nothing about רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון includes, without any limit, a חטאת whose owner gained atonement with another animal. So his son could follow that rule even in the blemish case. רבי can still hold that a backup does not die, and the answer of Step 6 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; maybe
Like his father
The five kinds of sin offerings that are left to die

steps.whatToRemember: רבי הושעיא follows רבי. A leftover חטאת dies only when it replaced a lost animal. A backup set aside from the start just grazes. The משנה of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון does not disprove this, because he may follow his father, רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, דִּלְמָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: No, perhaps Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
holds like his father,
who said: five sin offerings are left to die.
phrases.notes: This is the same rule of רבי שמעון mentioned in Step 5.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דִּלְמָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כַּאֲבוּהּ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption in Step 8 that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows רבי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the challenge of Steps 7-8 and keeps the answer of Step 6
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed the משנה follows רבי, but it could follow רבי שמעון instead.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the communal goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a communal חטאת is not left to die. This implies that an individual's חטאת in the same situation does die.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: 'Because a communal חטאת is not left to die.' This implies that an individual's חטאת is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to רבי הושעיא. It quotes a line from the משנה about the יום כיפור goats and draws out what it implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the leftover goat grazes only because it belongs to the community. That implies that if it were an individual's חטאת, it would die. The next step will show why this is a problem for רבי הושעיא.

keyTerms.meaning: A חטאת brought for the whole community
A חטאת brought by one person
Is left to die (locked away until it dies)
This implies (introduces an inference from the wording)

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין חַטַּאת צִבּוּר מֵתָה,
phrases.english: We learned: because a communal sin offering is not left to die,
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in יומא about the two goats of יום כיפור, when a second pair had to be brought.

phrases.english: this implies that an individual's is left to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין חַטַּאת צִבּוּר מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רבי הושעיא's ruling, which step 6 said follows רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי הושעיא's ruling that a leftover backup חטאת grazes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up the inference that an individual's leftover חטאת dies. The next step will show that the animal in this case counts as a backup.

steps.title: רב shows the leftover goat counts as a backup
steps.stepSummary: רב says living animals are not rejected, so the goat from the first pair may still be used. That makes the goat from the second pair a backup, and yet the משנה implies an individual's would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Living animals are not rejected. When he gets atonement, he may get atonement with the second goat of the first pair. So the other goat counts as a backup, and yet the משנה teaches that an individual's would die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. Using רב's ruling, it shows that the leftover goat in the משנה is like a backup, and an individual's backup would die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the first pair's goat is still valid, the goat from the second pair was not replacing a lost animal. It is just an extra backup. Yet the משנה implies an individual's leftover would die, which goes against רבי הושעיא, who said a backup grazes.

keyTerms.meaning: Living animals are not permanently rejected from being offered
The first pair of goats
A backup or guarantee, set aside in case the first is lost
And yet it teaches (points out a contradiction)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּין אֵינָן נִידְחִין,
phrases.english: Rav said: living animals are not rejected,
phrases.notes: He means the goat left from the first pair stays valid even though its partner died.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֵׁנִי שֶׁבְּזוּג רִאשׁוֹן מִתְכַּפֵּר,
phrases.english: so when he gets atonement, he may get atonement with the second goat of the first pair,
and the other one counts as a backup,
and yet it teaches that an individual's is left to die!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּין אֵינָן נִידְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי הושעיא's ruling that a backup חטאת grazes according to רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב, the second pair's goat is a backup. The משנה implies an individual's backup dies, which contradicts רבי הושעיא.

steps.title: רב follows his own view that the first must be used
steps.stepSummary: רב holds it is a מצוה to offer the first animal. So the second goat was known from the start not to be used, and it is not a true backup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב follows his own reasoning, since he said: The מצוה is to use the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In רב's view, the first animal must be used, so the extra goat is not a real backup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first must be offered, the second goat was never going to be used. That makes it like an animal set aside in place of a lost one, and in that case רבי holds the leftover dies. A true backup, where either animal may be used, still grazes, so רבי הושעיא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning stated elsewhere
It is a מצוה to offer the first animal that was set aside

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב admits a true backup dies. His point is that this goat was never a true backup, because the first one had to be used.

phrases.english: Rav follows his own reasoning,
since he said: the מצוה is with the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: מִצְוָה בָּרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 10-11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the second goat is not a true backup
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second pair's goat was a backup, so an individual's backup would die
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the first must be used, the second is like a replacement for a lost animal. A true backup still grazes according to רבי.
steps.whatToRemember: A true backup, where either animal may be used, grazes according to רבי. The יום כיפור case is different because, for רב, the first goat must be used.

steps.title: A ברייתא on when רבי and רבנן say the leftover dies
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר זירי teaches a ברייתא. If the animal was lost when the replacement was set aside, רבי says the leftover dies and רבנן say it grazes. If it was lost at the time of atonement, רבנן say it dies and רבי says it grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר זירי taught before רב פפא: If it was lost at the time of setting aside, according to רבי it dies and according to רבנן it grazes. If it was lost at the time of atonement, according to רבנן it dies and according to רבי it grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lays out the מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן. They disagree about which moment matters for leaving a leftover חטאת to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, what counts is whether the animal was missing when the replacement was set aside. If so, the leftover dies. For רבנן, what counts is whether it was missing when the other animal was offered. If so, it dies. Each side lets the leftover graze in the other side's case.

keyTerms.meaning: The time the replacement animal was set aside
The time atonement was achieved with the other animal
It grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold

steps.whyThisMatters: Read this version carefully: in the next step רב פפא shows with a קל וחומר that its second half cannot be right, and Step 15 corrects it so that everyone agrees an animal lost at the time of כפרה dies.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב שִׁימִי בַּר זֵירִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ziri taught before Rav Pappa:
If it was lost at the time of setting aside —
according to Rabbi it dies, according to the Rabbis it shall graze.
If it was lost at the time of atonement —
according to the Rabbis it dies, according to Rabbi it grazes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב שִׁימִי בַּר זֵירִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge is answered, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: lost at the time of setting aside, the leftover dies. Lost only at the time of atonement, it grazes. רבנן: the reverse.

steps.title: A קל וחומר shows the version of the ברייתא cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that if רבי is stricter in the easier case, he must also be strict in the harder case. So the version that has רבי saying 'grazes' at the time of כפרה makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's a קל וחומר: Look at an animal lost at the time the replacement was set aside. There the רבנן say it grazes, and still רבי says it dies. So take an animal lost at the time of כפרה, where even the רבנן say it dies. Isn't it obvious that רבי would also say it dies?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the version of the ברייתא that רב שימי בר זירי taught in Step 13. He uses a קל וחומר to show that רבי cannot hold 'grazes' in the case of loss at the time of כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'set aside' case, the רבנן are lenient (grazes) and רבי is strict (dies). In the 'atonement' case even the lenient רבנן are strict (dies). So the case of כפרה is clearly the harsher one, and רבי, who is strict even in the milder case, must surely be strict there too.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'all the more so' argument: if a rule holds in the milder case, it must hold in the stronger case
A lost animal
The time a replacement animal is set aside
The time the owner gains atonement by offering the replacement
It grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold
It is left to die

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two time points. 'Lost when set aside' means it was missing when the owner picked a replacement. 'Lost at the time of כפרה' means it was still missing when the replacement was actually offered.

phrases.english: It is a kal vachomer:
phrases.notes: רב פפא is saying this to רב שימי בר זירי to show that his version of the ברייתא from Step 13 can't be right.

phrases.english: Just as with an animal lost at the time of setting aside,
where the Rabbis say it grazes,
Rebbi says it dies —
then an animal lost at the time of atonement,
where according to the Rabbis it dies,
according to Rebbi, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the version of the ברייתא given in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling 'grazes' for an animal lost at the time of כפרה in רב שימי בר זירי's version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since רבי is strict in the milder 'set aside' case, where the רבנן are lenient, he must be strict in the 'atonement' case, where even the רבנן are strict. So he cannot say 'grazes' there.

steps.title: The corrected version of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is re-taught. If the animal was lost when the replacement was set aside, רבי says it dies and the רבנן say it grazes. If it was lost at the time of כפרה, everyone agrees it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, teach it like this: if it was lost at the time of setting aside, רבי says it dies and the רבנן say it grazes. If it was lost at the time of כפרה, everyone agrees it dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is fixed so that it no longer clashes with the קל וחומר. The argument stays only in the 'set aside' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא stays as it was. The second half changes: there is no longer a dispute about loss at the time of כפרה, because both sides agree the leftover animal dies. This removes the strange result of רבי being lenient in the harsher case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, teach it like this' — the ברייתא is re-taught in a corrected form
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: lost when the replacement was set aside → מחלוקת (רבי: dies, רבנן: grazes). Lost at the time of כפרה → everyone agrees it dies.

phrases.english: Rather, teach it like this:
if it was lost at the time of setting aside —
according to Rebbi it dies, according to the Rabbis it grazes.
If it was lost at the time of atonement —
everyone agrees it dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תָּנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of Step 14 by changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי and רבנן also argue about an animal lost at the time of כפרה, with רבי saying it grazes
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees an animal lost at the time of כפרה dies; the argument is only about loss at the time of setting aside

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view in the משנה, returning to the text of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the opening words of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's opinion. It is a short heading that marks a new section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, someone set aside a חטאת that got a blemish, so he sold it and brought another חטאת with the money. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says that if the second animal was offered before the first was slaughtered as regular food, the first is left to die, like a חטאת whose owner already got כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.' — the rest of the quote from the משנה is not written out

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the ברייתא and goes back to quote the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון in the משנה: if the replacement is offered before the blemished, sold animal is slaughtered, the first animal is left to die

steps.title: No skinning from the feet on יום טוב, or with a בכור or disqualified holy animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that you may not skin an animal from its feet on יום טוב. In the same way, you may not do this with a בכור or with פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one may not skin an animal starting from the feet on יום טוב. In the same way, one may not skin a בכור from the feet, and not פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a special way of skinning an animal, starting from the feet. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skinning from the feet keeps the hide in one piece, so it can be used as a container, for example a water skin. On יום טוב this is not allowed, even though plain skinning is allowed. The ברייתא compares a בכור and פסולי המוקדשין to יום טוב and forbids this way of skinning them too.

keyTerms.meaning: Skinning an animal starting from the feet, so the hide stays whole
Similarly; in the same way
A firstborn kosher animal, which is holy
Holy animals that became unfit for the altar (for example, through a blemish) and were redeemed

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One may not skin an animal from the feet on Yom Tov;
similarly —
one may not skin a firstborn animal from the feet,
nor disqualified consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Under the heading of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's opinion, brings a ברייתא whose ruling on פסולי המוקדשין will turn out to follow his view (step 21).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skinning from the feet is not allowed on יום טוב, and in the same way it is not allowed for a בכור or for פסולי המוקדשין

steps.title: The holiday rule makes sense, but who holds the firstborn rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts why skinning from the feet is forbidden on יום טוב, then asks which תנא forbids it for a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense on יום טוב, because he is putting in effort that the holiday does not need. But for a בכור, who taught this rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the יום טוב part of the ברייתא is easy to understand. It now asks which תנא would forbid skinning a בכור from its feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב the reason is simple: skinning this way is extra work that is not needed for the holiday. With a blemished בכור there is no holiday issue, so the גמרא wants to know whose opinion treats it so strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (accepts one part before asking about another)
Effort, exertion
A firstborn animal, which is holy and given to a כהן
Which תנא taught this? (asks whose opinion a teaching follows)

phrases.english: Granted, on a Festival,
since he exerts effort
that is not fit for it,
phrases.notes: He means effort the holiday does not need.

phrases.english: but a firstborn: who taught this?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a בכור may not be skinned from its feet?

steps.title: The firstborn rule follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the בכור rule is the view of בית שמאי, who hold that a בכור keeps its holiness even after it gets a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is בית שמאי, who say a בכור stays in its holiness. As we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say an ordinary Jew may not be counted together with a כהן to eat a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question from Step 18. He says the ruling follows בית שמאי and brings a משנה to show their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, a blemished בכור is still holy, so only כהנים may eat it. Since it keeps its holiness, it cannot be treated like ordinary meat, and that explains why it may not be skinned from the feet.

keyTerms.meaning: It remains in its holiness
May not be counted (as a partner in eating)
A priest

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: It is Beit Shammai,
who say: a firstborn remains in its sanctity,
as we learned: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִמָּנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם הַכֹּהֵן עַל הַבְּכוֹר.
phrases.english: An Israelite may not be counted with the priest for the firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכור ruling follows בית שמאי, who hold that a blemished בכור keeps its holiness.

steps.title: Who holds the rule for disqualified sacrifices?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא forbids skinning פסולי המוקדשין from the feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Disqualified sacrificial animals: who taught this rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last part of the ברייתא and asks the same question about פסולי המוקדשין. It is setting up רב חסדא's next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין are holy animals that got a blemish and were redeemed, so usually they can be treated like ordinary meat. The גמרא wants to know who still treats them strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy animals that became unfit for the altar, usually because of a blemish, and were redeemed

phrases.english: Disqualified consecrated animals: who taught this?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין, מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question to Step 18, now about the third case in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that פסולי המוקדשין may not be skinned from the feet?

steps.title: It follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, with a teaching about two sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the ruling is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's and starts quoting a ברייתא about two חטאות, one unblemished and one blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. As a ברייתא teaches: If a person had two חטאות, one unblemished and one blemished, the unblemished one is brought on the altar and the blemished one is redeemed. If the blemished one was slaughtered before the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled, it is permitted. If it was slaughtered after the blood was sprinkled, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון as the source and begins quoting a ברייתא. Here the ברייתא gives the basic case of two חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing of the sprinkling matters. Before the blood of the unblemished חטאת is sprinkled, the redeemed blemished animal is permitted. Once the sprinkling has happened, the owner already got his כפרה through the other animal, so the blemished one becomes forbidden. The next step quotes the line of the ברייתא that ties it to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering
Unblemished, fit for the altar
An animal with a blemish
It shall be redeemed (its holiness moved onto money)
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, the step that brings כפרה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the blemished animal is forbidden because of its blemish. It is forbidden only if it is slaughtered after the other חטאת's blood is sprinkled, because by then the owner already got his כפרה.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
It is Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
as it is taught: If there were two sin offerings before him,
one unblemished and one blemished,
the unblemished one is sacrificed,
the blemished one is redeemed.
If the blemished one was slaughtered,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — מוּתֶּרֶת;
phrases.english: before the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled, it is permitted;
after the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: By then the owner got his כפרה through the other animal, so this one is now treated as a leftover חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 and begins bringing a supporting ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסולי המוקדשין ruling follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, supported by a ברייתא about two חטאות.
steps.raayaObject: That the ruling on פסולי המוקדשין follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two חטאות, one unblemished and one blemished

steps.title: Even the cooking meat of the blemished animal must be burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון rules that once the unblemished חטאת's blood is sprinkled, the blemished animal's meat must be burned. This is true even if that meat is already in the pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: even if the meat of the blemished animal is already in the pot, once the blood of the unblemished animal is sprinkled, the meat goes to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that רב חסדא began in the previous step. This is the line that shows what רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blemished חטאת was redeemed, and its meat is already being cooked. Even so, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it must be burned once the owner gets atonement through the other animal. So he holds that redeemed פסולי המוקדשין still keep holiness. That is why he would forbid skinning them from the feet.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish, here the blemished חטאת
Unblemished, here the healthy חטאת
Cooking pot
Its blood was sprinkled on the מזבח
The place where disqualified קדשים are burned

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the proof behind רב חסדא's claim that the פסולי המוקדשין part of the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if the meat of the blemished one is in the pot,
and the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled,
it goes out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רב חסדא began quoting in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the פסולי המוקדשין rule follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires burning the redeemed blemished חטאת's meat

steps.title: Why not attribute both rules to בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא did not simply say both rules follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא: let him establish both this one and that one according to בית שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא for using two different תנאים. It suggests he could have used only בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that a blemished בכור stays holy. So maybe they also hold that blemished פסולי המוקדשין stay holy. If so, one תנא would explain the whole ברייתא, which is simpler than splitting it.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him establish it, meaning attribute the ruling to a certain opinion
This one and that one, meaning both rulings

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda, let him establish
both this and that according to Beit Shammai!
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the בכור rule and the פסולי המוקדשין rule from the ברייתא in step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא, לוֹקְמַהּ אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's choice to split the ברייתא between two תנאים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's attribution of the פסולי המוקדשין rule to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One תנא, בית שמאי, could explain both rulings, so there is no need for two.

steps.title: בית שמאי may only speak about a בכור, which is holy from birth
steps.stepSummary: Maybe בית שמאי's view applies only to a בכור, because its holiness starts in the womb. They may not say the same about פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps when בית שמאי said it, it was about a בכור, whose holiness is from the womb. But about פסולי המוקדשין, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It explains why בית שמאי cannot automatically be used for the second rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור becomes holy by itself at birth. Other קדשים became holy only because a person set them aside. So בית שמאי might say a בכור's holiness is stronger and stays even after a blemish. But they might not say that about redeemed פסולי המוקדשין.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
Firstborn animal, which is holy from birth
Its holiness comes from the womb, meaning from birth
קדשים that got a blemish and were redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור's holiness comes from birth, so it may be stronger than the holiness of other קדשים.

phrases.english: Perhaps when Beit Shammai said it,
it was about a firstborn, whose holiness is from the womb,
but disqualified consecrated animals, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כִּי אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (בכור versus פסולי המוקדשין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי's view about a blemished בכור applies to all blemished קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי may limit their view to a בכור, whose holiness comes from birth, so רב חסדא needed a different תנא for פסולי המוקדשין.

steps.title: Why not attribute both rules to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the opposite question: why not say both rules follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him establish both this one and that one according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא again, this time from the other side. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that even redeemed פסולי המוקדשין keep their holiness. A בכור's holiness is even stronger, so he should surely say the same about a בכור. Then he alone could explain the whole ברייתא, without needing בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of

phrases.english: And let him establish both this and that
according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַאּ אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 24's answer around: since a בכור's holiness is even stronger, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון should cover both rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's attribution of the בכור rule to בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If redeemed פסולי המוקדשין keep their holiness for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, then a בכור surely does too, so one תנא is enough.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's view may apply only to disqualified consecrated animals
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strict view applies only to פסולי המוקדשין, whose holiness passes onto their redemption money, and not to a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps when רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said his ruling, he meant only disqualified consecrated animals, whose holiness is strong enough to pass onto their redemption money. For a בכור, he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 25. We cannot say both rules follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, because his view may cover only פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין can be redeemed, and their holiness is strong enough to transfer onto the money. A בכור cannot be redeemed at all. So רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strictness may not carry over to a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals that became unfit for the altar, usually because of a blemish
Redemption: paying money so the holiness moves from the animal onto the money
To 'catch' or take hold of, meaning the holiness passes onto something else
A firstborn male animal, holy from birth, which cannot be redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's view may fit only a בכור, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view may fit only פסולי המוקדשין. That is why רב חסדא needed both sources.

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן —
phrases.english: Perhaps when Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, said it,
it was about disqualified consecrated animals,
which are strong enough to pass their holiness onto their redemption money,
but about a firstborn, he did not say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 25 using the same kind of reasoning as Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a תנא's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One source, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, could cover both the בכור and פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.terutzMaskana: His view may apply only to redeemable animals whose holiness passes onto the money, so a separate source is needed for a בכור.

steps.title: Challenge from the rule allowing sale in the butchers' market
steps.stepSummary: A משנה lets פסולי המוקדשין be sold like regular meat so they bring more money. So רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון should also allow flaying from the feet, which raises the price.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון not accept the משנה that says all פסולי המוקדשין are slaughtered and sold in the butchers' market and weighed by the litra? We see that once you allow this, the meat sells for more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון with a משנה. That משנה lets people treat פסולי המוקדשין like regular meat because it earns the Temple more money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows a principle: whatever raises the selling price helps the Temple, so it is permitted. Flaying from the feet keeps the hide whole and raises the price. By that logic, it should also be allowed for פסולי המוקדשין.

keyTerms.meaning: The butchers' market, where regular meat is sold to many buyers
A litra, a unit of weight used to sell regular meat
'Apparently' or 'we see from here', used to draw a conclusion
More (here: a higher price)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לֵית לֵיהּ
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, not hold
that which we learned in a mishnah:
All disqualified consecrated animals
are slaughtered in the butchers' market
and sold in the butchers' market
and weighed by the litra?
Apparently, once you permit it,
it sells for more!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לֵית לֵיהּ הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ruling is tied to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון for פסולי המוקדשין, the גמרא tests whether his strictness fits a known משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's apparent ban on flaying פסולי המוקדשין from the feet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits treating פסולי המוקדשין like regular meat because it raises the price for the Temple. Flaying from the feet also raises the price, so it should be permitted too.

steps.title: Saving the hide ruins the meat
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא answers that what improves the hide damages the meat, so flaying from the feet does not really raise the total price.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, son of רב כהנא, said: what improves the hide damages the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the challenge from Step 27. Flaying from the feet does not actually bring the Temple more money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To keep the hide whole, you end up cutting away some of the meat. What you gain on the hide, you lose on the meat. Since the total price does not go up, the reasoning of the butchers'-market משנה does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Improves, adds value
Hide, skin of the animal
Damages, lowers the value

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said:
What improves the hide
damages the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27 by denying that flaying from the feet increases the profit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: there is no real gain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flaying from the feet raises the price, just like selling in the butchers' market.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gain on the hide is cancelled by the loss on the meat, so there is no reason to permit it.

steps.title: In the West: it looks like working with holy animals
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they gave a different reason in the name of רבי אבין: flaying from the feet looks like doing work with holy animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they said in the name of רבי אבין: it is because it looks like doing work with holy animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different answer to the challenge from Step 27. This one comes from the sages of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not argue about money at all. Even if flaying from the feet did earn more, it is forbidden because it looks like using holy animals for work. Doing work with קדשים is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The West', meaning ארץ ישראל (west of Bavel)
Doing work with, or using, holy animals, which is forbidden
Looks like, gives the appearance of

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons not to flay פסולי המוקדשין from the feet. The first is practical: nothing is gained, because the meat is damaged. The second is about appearance: it looks like doing work with holy animals.

phrases.english: In the West they said in the name of Rabbi Avin:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which is west of Bavel.

phrases.english: Because it looks
like doing work with holy animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to Step 27, in place of רב מרי's money-based answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason for the ban: appearance of forbidden use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If flaying from the feet earns more money, it should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden anyway, because it looks like doing work with holy animals.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree so people won't raise whole flocks
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין gives another reason for the ban on flaying from the feet. It is a rabbinic גזירה, so that people won't end up raising large flocks of פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: It is a rabbinic decree, so that a person will not end up raising many flocks of these animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more answer to the question of why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון forbids flaying from the feet. רבי יוסי בר אבין says the rule is a rabbinic safeguard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי said flaying from the feet doesn't really earn more money, and רבי אבין said it looks like working with holy animals. רבי יוסי בר אבין gives a third answer: the ban is a גזירה. Without it, someone might keep these holy animals around instead of slaughtering them, and they would multiply into big flocks. That makes it likely he will come to shear them or work with them, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a fence, so people don't come to break a real prohibition
Lest; out of concern that
He will raise or breed
Many flocks; literally 'flocks, flocks'

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations for the ban on flaying from the feet. רב מרי says it doesn't really raise the total price. רבי אבין says it looks like working with holy animals. רבי יוסי בר אבין says it is a גזירה, so people won't raise whole flocks of פסולי המוקדשין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
It is a decree, lest he raise
from them many, many flocks.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר: גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third answer, alongside רב מרי (Step 28) and רבי אבין (Step 29), to the question in Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason: the ban is a rabbinic גזירה, not a matter of price.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since flaying from the feet raises the price, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון should allow it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if it raises the price, the Rabbis banned it so people won't keep these animals and raise flocks of them, which could lead to shearing or working them.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter ולד חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the chapter ולד חטאת with the traditional Hadran formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'ולד חטאת'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter ולד חטאת. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Hadran is a traditional closing line said when finishing a chapter. It expresses that we hope to come back and learn this chapter again. The discussion about פסולי המוקדשין ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the traditional line that closes a chapter
The offspring of a חטאת; the name of this chapter, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'The offspring of a sin offering.'
phrases.notes: Chapters are named by their first words, so this is the name of the chapter we just finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ וְלַד חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last explanation in Step 30.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter ולד חטאת is finished.
